title: Sum of K-Times Consecutive Runs
statement:
You are given an array of `n` integers and an integer `k`. A **run** is a maximal block of equal values sitting next to each other (a block that cannot be extended to the left or right with the same value).

Find the sum of the numbers that appear consecutively **exactly `k` times**: every run whose length is exactly `k` contributes its value once to the sum. Runs of any other length contribute nothing. If the same value forms two separate runs of length `k`, each run counts, so the value is added twice. If no run has length `k`, the answer is `0`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers: the array.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the sum.

examples.explanation: The runs are 1 (length 2), 2 (length 3) and 3 (length 2). Only the runs of 1 and 3 have length exactly 2, so the sum is 1 + 3 = 4.
The runs of length 1 are the single 6 and the single 8, giving 14. The runs of 5 and 7 have length 2 and are ignored.
The runs are 4 (length 2), 9 (length 1), 4 (length 2), 9 (length 1). The value 4 forms two separate runs of length 2, so it is added twice: 4 + 4 = 8.

hints: Walk through the array and measure the length of each maximal block of equal values.
When a block ends (the next element differs or the array ends), check whether its length equals k.
Add the value, not the length, and remember to handle the last block after the loop.
